title: The cutover extract format, the cutover record and the field list beyond the AC wording are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC1, AC3 and Data table; FSD P1 v3 A2.2 (DP05 row) and A2.11; TSD P1 v3 T3.3 and T3.6
section: Legacy RWB-DM-005; FSD P1 v3 A2.2, A2.11; TSD P1 v3 T3.3, T3.6
description: The legacy story requires the open promises and contact notes held outside EFS to be migrated to the case and requires ten clean days before the sign-off, and it names three tables with their field ranges. No source gives the extract's record format, its file name or the identity that reads it, the field list it carries beyond the five facts of AC1 and the fourteen contact point fields of the data row, or the shape and place of the cutover record that holds the ten day rows and the sign-off. The load's own record of what it read is therefore agreed at the cutover rehearsal and cited, not invented.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC1 ('each interaction keeps its case, its person_key, its contact_key, its promise date and its promise amount') and AC3 ('ten clean days'); Data table rows recovery_case DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-055, interaction DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-029, contact_point_ext DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026. Architecture v5 slide 32 puts cutover loads under one-off bulk work with no format given.
proposed: The extract is a one-off read of the legacy cutover dump with the legacy record key as its idempotency key, and the cutover record is the record of the release pipeline that holds the counts, the ten day rows and the sign-off; formats, file name and dump layout are fixed at the cutover rehearsal and recorded in this story's Flyway description.

title: The legacy interaction carries person_key and contact_key while the ledger table has party_id and contact_point_id and no P1 DDL
source: Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC1 and Data table (interaction DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-029); TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (interaction); Ownership Map v1 interaction (owner P1, ASM-A6-tables-1); TSD P1 v3 T3.6 (no interaction entry)
section: Legacy RWB-DM-005; TSD P3 v3 T3.1; TSD P1 v3 T3.5, T3.6
description: The legacy AC1 keeps 'its person_key and its contact_key' on each migrated interaction. The only column list of the table says party_id and contact_point_id, both cross-references, and contact_point_id points at a Workbench contact row that no longer exists in the target, where a contact is an ACE record with a business key and an extension row. The table is P1's by the Ownership Map ruling but is defined only in the P3 TSD, and the P1 TSD lists thirteen P1 tables and does not include it, so neither the DDL the load writes against nor the way the two business keys are held on the row is stated by one source.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC1 and Data table; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 interaction fields DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-029 (party_id DF-INT-003, contact_point_id DF-INT-022); Ownership Map interaction owner P1 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-1; TSD P1 v3 T3.5 contact_point_ext keyed by contact_key and T3.9 business-key links.
proposed: The migrated row keeps person_key and contact_key as ACE business keys and resolves no cross-reference of its own: no party_id and no contact_point_id is invented, and the P1 DB story that owns the table confirms the two business-key columns when it aligns the table with TSD P3 v3 T3.1.

title: contact_point_ext is DP02's Workbench table in the FSD while the legacy DM-005 data row and this cutover slice carry it
source: FSD P1 v3 A2.2 (DP02 and DP05 rows); legacy RWB-DM-005 Data table; TSD P1 v3 T3.5; Ownership Map v1 contact_point_ext (owner P1)
section: FSD P1 v3 A2.2; legacy RWB-DM-005 Data table; TSD P1 v3 T3.5
description: The FSD gives contact_point_ext to data product DP02 Customer and party, together with party_ext, and gives DP05 Contact and promises only interaction as its Workbench table. The legacy RWB-DM-005 data row nevertheless lists contact_point_ext with DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026, so the legacy key's cutover carries the consent and contact-quality rows the Workbench held about ACE contacts. No source says which target slice writes those rows at cutover, and RWB-P1-DM002-APP builds the read path over the table and writes none of it.
evidence: FSD P1 v3 A2.2 table: DP02 row 'party_ext, contact_point_ext'; DP05 row 'interaction'. Legacy RWB-DM-005 Data table: contact_point_ext DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026. TSD P1 v3 T3.5 contact_point_ext fields and the consent mapping. Ownership Map contact_point_ext owner P1.
proposed: The DM-005 cutover load writes the legacy consent and contact-quality rows into contact_point_ext because the legacy key carries them, RWB-P1-DM002-APP reads them for DP02 and writes none, and the DP05 catalog definition keeps interaction as its only Workbench table.

title: The rows of the legacy migration are split across P1 and S5, the case asset link has no table in the target, and no single source gives the extract, handover or field list
source: Ownership Map v1 listing, asset_sale, valuation_ext and recovery_case; legacy RWB-DM-006 AC1, Data table and guardrails; TSD P1 v3 T3.0, T3.2 and T3.5; LDM v8 table inventory and DF-EXT-036 to DF-EXT-049
section: Ownership Map; legacy RWB-DM-006; sections 1, 3, 4, 11, 12.7 and 13 of RWB-P1-DM006-APP
description: The legacy story moves the listing, the case asset link, the sale instruction and the appraisal acceptance in one cutover and asserts only that each listing and each sale carries its asset_key, each appraisal decision its valuation_key, and that no collateral, appraisal, NPA asset or NPA sale record is copied. The Ownership Map then splits the rows three ways: listing and asset_sale are S5 rwb-asset's in rwb_asset, valuation_ext is P1's in rwb_source_data as one of the four Tier 3 extension tables keyed 1:1 on valuation_key, and recovery_case is P3 rwb-case's. No source says which service loads which rows, what the handover between P1 and S5 looks like, or what the extract carries beyond the AC wording. Three further readings have no single source: the legacy case asset link has no object of its own in LDM v8 or in the Ownership Map, so its home in the target is unsettled; the legacy guardrail requires a migrated record to keep its source and its migration date, while valuation_ext carries only the seven standard columns of TSD P1 v3 T3.0 and listing and asset_sale carry none in LDM v8 DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-019; and the appraisal acceptance table is created by the V0001 baseline rather than by the cutover version, so the load has to be an idempotent insert on an existing table rather than a schema change.
evidence: Ownership Map: listing owner S5 (Architecture v5 slide 41, TSD S5 v2 T3.1); asset_sale owner S5, same basis; valuation_ext owner P1 with ruling that it stays one of the four extension tables (FSD P1 v3, TSD P1 v3, ASM-A6-tables-15); recovery_case owner P3. Legacy RWB-DM-006 AC1 'Then each listing and each sale carries its asset_key, and each appraisal decision its valuation_key'; Data table recovery_case DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-055, listing DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008, asset_sale DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019, valuation_ext DF-EXT-036 to DF-EXT-049; guardrails 'A migrated record keeps its source and its migration date, and never a copy of an ACE row'. TSD P1 v3 T3.2 'V0001 baseline | 92 tables, the dictionary seed, v_data_dictionary'; T3.5 'DF-EXT-043 to 049 are the standard columns'. LDM v8 lists no case_asset object and no source or migrated_at column on listing, asset_sale or valuation_ext.
owner_role: Solution architect with the data steward and the S5 rwb-asset tech lead
proposed: P1 extracts the four row groups, loads the appraisal acceptances into valuation_ext through its own version idempotently on valuation_key, and hands the listing, the sale and the case asset link to S5 in one package per cutover business date; S5 loads them into rwb_asset on S5's own sequence; the case asset link is carried on the handover row as the case key beside the asset_key and lands in no table of its own; and the source tag and the cutover business date ride on the handover row and in the Flyway history description because no column carries them.

title: No source defines a clean day for a WEEKLY product, or where the ten day count and the sign-off are kept
source: Legacy RWB-DM-006 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.2, A2.11.2, A2.12, A2.13 and A2.14.2; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 reconciliation_result; Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-04
description: AC3 requires ten clean days on the migrated records before the data steward signs off, and it names neither what makes a day clean nor where the count and the sign-off are kept. The two sources that touch the question do not meet: DP06 Collateral and assets is refreshed WEEKLY and expected by MON 08:00 from CCMS, SVAF, AMIS and RPS, and it is STALE while any of those sources is late, while JOB-04 runs daily on the ACE batch record and writes one reconciliation_result row per check and product group. A day can therefore pass REC-01 and REC-05 with a DP06 stamp whose oldest source business date is a week old, and no source says whether such a day counts. The retention window of the legacy tables is likewise named by AC3 without a period, and no table is given for the counter or the sign-off.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-006 AC3 'Given ten clean days on the migrated records / When the data steward signs off / Then the legacy tables stay read-only for their retention period'. FSD P1 v3 DP06 row 'ACE (ingested from CCMS, SVAF, AMIS and RPS) | v_ace_collateral, v_ace_asset, v_ace_collateral_detail, v_ace_valuation, v_ace_npa_asset, v_ace_npa_sale | valuation_ext, listing, asset_sale | WEEKLY | MON 08:00'; A2.14.2 'When the cut-off for a product (data_product.expected_by) passes before its batch completes, or the batch fails, EV-27 AceDataLate is published and the product is flagged STALE'; BR-P1-014-3 'A product fed by more than one source carries the oldest business date among its sources'; A2.11.2 'Writes reconciliation_result per check and product group; lists the breaks for the data steward'; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 reconciliation_result DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129; DL25 answer A 'zero; any difference holds the publish'.
owner_role: Data steward with the P1 reconciliation owner and the release manager
proposed: Count ten clean days from the reconciliation_result rows of JOB-04 on the migrated records: a PASS day with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan on a LOADED DP06 stamp counts, a BREAK row, a new orphan or a STALE DP06 day resets the count to zero, and a day whose DP06 stamp is STALE is never counted as clean; hold the ten day rows, the DP06 stamps and the sign-off in the cutover record of the release pipeline and create no counter table and no sign-off table.

title: The valuation_key proof and the DP06 freshness read depend on Section B views that ship with RWB-ACE-001, and no source says how the cutover behaves before that week
source: TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.3 views 18 and 17; FSD P1 v3 OQ-P1-01, OQ-P1-02 and A2.14.2; Decision Log DL43; legacy RWB-DM-006 AC1
description: AC1 rests on two Section B views. v_ace_valuation is view 18, over the Tier 2 table valuation, keyed by valuation_key, so the valuation_key proof has no live source until RWB-ACE-001 is deployed; v_ace_batch_status is view 17, and DP06's freshness stamp and the STALE flag are read from it, so the DP06 stamp is STALE for every product until the same week. TSD P1 v3 ships the 14 Section B views the week RWB-ACE-001 is deployed and keeps the features that read them behind a feature flag, and FSD P1 v3 records both open points with the ACE team lead as owner. DL43 sets 2026-11-21 for a 30 November release, which is before this story's own release, but no source states what the cutover does with the two reads in the gap: whether the appraisal acceptance rows are loaded at all, whether the key can be counted as proved against a fake, and whether a day can ever be clean while the DP06 stamp is STALE.
evidence: TSD P1 v3 T3.2 'Section B (proposed V0003, next free sequence after RWB-ACE-001) | 14 views over the Tier 2 tables | Ships The week RWB-ACE-001 is deployed (DL43) | Until it ships: Features that read a Section B view stay behind their feature flag; the freshness stamp falls back to STALE for every product (T3.7)'; T3.3 view 17 v_ace_batch_status key 'source_system, business_date' and view 18 v_ace_valuation key 'valuation_key'; FSD P1 v3 OQ-P1-01 'v_ace_batch_status is a Section B view, so freshness (A2.14) and every job that starts on the ACE batch record depend on it'; OQ-P1-02 'Freshness before RWB-ACE-001 lands'; A2.14.2 DP06 sources CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS; Decision Log DL43 'the date is 2026-11-21 for a 30 November release'.
area: ACE dependency, freshness and feature flags
owner_role: Solution architect with the ACE team lead and the data steward
proposed: Prove asset_key against v_ace_asset and v_ace_collateral from Day 1, prove valuation_key against v_ace_valuation from the week RWB-ACE-001 lands and against its contract fake before, load the appraisal acceptance rows in both cases because they are Workbench decisions keyed by an ACE business key with no foreign key, and keep the cutover behind its feature switch until the Section B views answer so that no day is counted clean on a STALE DP06 stamp.

title: Three services own the legal action, notice and instruction rows of one legacy key, and no source fixes the handover package format or which keys travel beyond the legacy AC wording
source: Ownership Map on legal_action (S4, rwb_litigation), notice (P6, rwb_comms) and partner_instruction (S9, rwb_partner); legacy RWB-DM-007 Data table, Endpoints and guardrails; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 45; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.3 views 22 to 24; split plan of RWB-P1-DM007-APP
description: The legacy story migrates legal_action, notice and partner_instruction as one cutover step run by the recovery service identity in the single recovery schema, and reads the court record from v_ace_lawsuit and v_ace_hearing. The Ownership Map splits the three tables across S4, P6 and S9, each in its own schema with its own login and its own Flyway sequence under DP-15, and DP-01 forbids a cross-schema write, so one service can no longer move all three. No source states the shape of a handover package, how many packages leave per cutover business date, where in the release pipeline they are written, or which key accompanies each record so that the owner can join it to its case and its ACE row: the legacy AC wording names the case, the court, the claim, the judgment, the person_key, the firm and the due date and stops there, and the data table gives field ranges only. The cutover dump layout, its file name and the identity that may read it are likewise absent from every source.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-007 Endpoints: No endpoint in this story. The migration is a cutover step run by the recovery service identity, and its breaks are listed on the reconciliation extract.; Data table legal_action DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014, notice DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-034, partner_instruction DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016; guardrail No read of another module's tables and a migrated record keeps its source and its migration date; Ownership Map legal_action owner S4 on Architecture v5 slide 41 and TSD S4 v2 T3.1, notice owner P6, partner_instruction owner S9, all three with an empty ruling; Architecture v5 slide 45 Who reads ACE's data? Only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views (ADR-010); TSD P1 v3 T3.3 marks views 22, 23 and 24 Section B; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 ships Section B with RWB-ACE-001.
proposed: P1 reads the legacy cutover dump once, maps each record to its case and its ACE business keys and hands one package per owner per cutover business date; S4, P6 and S9 load their own rows on their own Flyway sequences and P1 writes no other service's schema; the package layout and the cutover record are agreed at the cutover rehearsal and the extract carries the legacy keys only.

title: partner_instruction sits in the data table of two legacy keys and no source rules which facts each migration slice carries
source: Legacy RWB-DM-007 and RWB-DM-008 Data tables; Ownership Map partner_instruction (S9, rwb_partner); FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP07 and DP08 rows
description: Both legacy keys list partner_instruction: RWB-DM-007 as the law firm instruction raised for a legal action, with its firm and its due date named in AC1, and RWB-DM-008 as the panel record with the firms, their users and their open instructions so that panel status and performance continue across cutover. The table is S9's in rwb_partner and S9 loads it once, so the same instruction would be handed over twice. No source states which facts belong to the legal slice and which to the panel slice, whether one load completes the row from two packages or one package carries the whole row, or what makes the second load idempotent. The data product table does not settle it either: DP08 Partner performance names partner and partner_instruction, while DP07 Legal events and cases names legal_action, notice and hearing.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-007 Data table partner_instruction DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 with AC1 each instruction its firm and its due date; legacy RWB-DM-008 story As a data steward, I want the panel firms, their users and their open instructions migrated from the legacy Workbench, so that panel status and performance continue across cutover; FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP07 row over v_ace_lawsuit, v_ace_hearing, v_ace_pod and legal_action, notice, hearing, and DP08 row over partner, partner_instruction; Ownership Map partner_instruction owner S9 with an empty ruling.
proposed: RWB-P1-DM007-APP hands over the instruction raised for a legal action with the instruction id, the case, the firm, the instruction type, the instructed_at and the due_at; RWB-P1-DM008-APP hands over the panel performance facts of the same instruction; S9 loads both packages, idempotent on the instruction id.

title: The ten clean days, the sign-off record, the read-only window and the feature-switch default are stated as outcomes and fixed by no source
source: Legacy RWB-DM-007 AC3, Screen and states and guardrails; FSD P1 v3 A2.11 and A2.13; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 reconciliation_result DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 32 and 44; Template and Rules §R5.5
description: AC3 says ten clean days, a sign-off, a read-only legacy table set and a new schema, and names no mechanism, no record and no period. No source states which rows the count reads, whether a break resets the count or blocks the sign-off outright, where the sign-off and the ten day rows are kept, how long the legacy tables stay read-only, or what the feature switch of the cutover defaults to when the release pipeline first runs it. The sibling migration slices of RWB-SVC-P1 face the same gap, so one mechanism is applied across the family and recorded once per slice.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-007 AC3 Given ten clean days on the migrated records / When the data steward signs off / Then the legacy tables stay read-only for their retention period / And the migrated records are served from the new schema; Screen and states SCR-45 Data quality, Loading and breaks; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.2 writes reconciliation_result per check and product group and lists the breaks for the data steward; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 result LOV varchar(8) over PASS and BREAK; Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-04 Reconciliation owned by rwb-source-data as an event-triggered workflow; Template and Rules §R1 U7 dates unchanged and tentative.
proposed: The count reads the reconciliation_result rows JOB-04 writes for the migrated records per business date; a PASS row with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan extends the count and a BREAK row or a new orphan resets it to zero; the ten day rows and the sign-off sit in the cutover record of the release pipeline beside the read-only window; the flag rwb.source-data.dm007-cutover-extract defaults off.

title: The DM007 and DM008 instruction slice, the handover package format, the recency proof of a product with no ACE view and the field list beyond AC1 are not fixed by one source
source: Legacy RWB-DM-007 and RWB-DM-008 in 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3.md (lines 381 to 547); FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.2.2 (the DP08 row), A2.11 and A2.14; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.2, T3.6, T3.7 and Appendix T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 32, 41, 44 and 45; split plan metadata of RWB-P1-DM008-APP
description: Four things this story builds have no single source. First, RWB-DM-007 and RWB-DM-008 both carry partner_instruction DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016: DM007 AC1 reads each instruction with its firm and its due date and DM008 AC1 reads the same instruction with its case and its result, and no source says which key hands over which facts or how the two packages meet. Second, the handover package has no definition at all: no source fixes its format, its field order, its record layout, its file name or the point at which it leaves P1, although the cutover and the S9 load both depend on that shape. Third, DP08 has no ACE source view and no data_product_load stamp (the FSD product table gives it the Workbench as its system of record and the refresh cycle ON_CHANGE, and TSD T3.7 lists DP08 among the Workbench products), so the recency of the migrated records cannot be proved by a freshness stamp and no source states what AC3's ten clean days are measured on for this product. Fourth, the legacy data row names six of the seven partner fields, five of the six partner user fields and six of the nine instruction fields, while AC1 reads the score and the result as the remaining facts and the DP08 row names partner and partner_instruction and does not carry partner_user at all.
evidence: RWB-DM-007 data row: partner_instruction id, case_id, partner_id, instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at and 3 more | DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016; RWB-DM-008 data row: the same range, with partner DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 and partner_user DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217; FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP08 Partner performance | Workbench | None | partner, partner_instruction | ON_CHANGE | As it changes; TSD P1 v3 T3.7 product-to-source row: DP03, DP04, DP08, DP09, DP10, DP12 and DP14 are Workbench products, refreshed on change, with no source in v_ace_batch_status; legacy AC3: Given ten clean days on the migrated records, When the data steward signs off.
area: Data scope, cutover evidence and handover
owner_role: Data steward and data product owner of rwb-source-data with the S9 rwb-partner tech lead and the data migration lead
proposed: Rule the instruction slice at the cutover rehearsal: this key hands over the panel, the partner users and the performance facts of the instructions, RWB-DM-007 hands over the instructions raised for legal actions, and S9 loads both idempotently on the instruction id; fix the package layout and the handover point in the cutover record; count the ten clean days from the reconciliation_result rows of JOB-04 for the business dates after the load, a PASS row with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan per day, with a break resetting the count; and carry the three legacy field ranges whole so that the field list beyond AC1 is the legacy dictionary's and not the story's.

title: RWB-ITG-DM008-ITG states that the cutover load into rwb_partner runs on P1's own Flyway sequence, which DP-01 and the Ownership Map forbid
source: RWB-ITG-DM008-ITG sections 1, 2, 11, 13 and 19 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-ITG-W4 Wave 4 integration); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json tables partner, partner_user and partner_instruction; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29, 41 and 45; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15; split plan rows RWB-P1-DM008-APP and RWB-ITG-DM008-ITG
description: The wave 4 integration story of the same legacy key asserts twice that the cutover load of the partner, partner user and partner instruction records into rwb_partner is P1's own cutover migration on P1's own Flyway sequence. The Ownership Map gives partner, partner_user and partner_instruction to S9 rwb-partner in schema rwb_partner, the partner-user ruling ASM-A6-tables-6 keeps the users with S9 rather than P4, and DP-01 forbids a service from reading or writing another service's tables; Architecture v5 slide 29 enforces that ownership by grants and slide 45 keeps a single reader of the ACE views. Read literally, the integration story would have P1 own a sequence in rwb_partner, which contradicts both the ownership ruling and the boundary the architecture test enforces. The split plan gives both slices DP-15, and the P1 slice must therefore state which service loads.
evidence: RWB-ITG-DM008-ITG section 1: The real firms, their users and their instructions are loaded by P1's own cutover migration on its own Flyway sequence (DP-15); section 19: The cutover load of the records into rwb_partner is P1's own Flyway sequence; Ownership Map: partner | owner S9 | basis Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 and slide 17 S9 DB line, TSD S9 v2 T3.1; partner_user | owner S9 | ruling Partner users stay with S9 rwb-partner, despite TSD P4 v3 defining partner_user (ASM-A6-tables-6); DP-01: Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables.
owner_role: Solution architect with the S9 rwb-partner and P1 rwb-source-data tech leads
proposed: Read the integration story's sentence as the handover and not as a P1 write: P1 extracts and hands over one package per cutover business date, S9 rwb-partner loads rwb_partner on S9's own Flyway sequence, and P1's version creates no table in that schema. Correct the two sentences in RWB-ITG-DM008-ITG at the next revision, and let the S9 load story carry the sequence and the idempotency on the instruction id.

title: debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account are S6's while the legacy migration and its AC1 and AC3 sit on the P1 slice, and no source says who loads
source: Ownership Map v1 debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account (owner S6); Architecture v5 slide 41 (S6 owns lots, data room, buyer terms, bids, award, transfer); legacy RWB-DM-009 Data table; RWB-ITG-DM009-ITG section 1
section: Ownership Map; legacy RWB-DM-009 sections 1, 7 and 11
description: The legacy story sits in the P1 Recovery data engine module and migrates debt_sale_lot, debt_sale_account and recovery_case. The Ownership Map puts both debt sale tables with S6 rwb-debtsale in rwb_debtsale and recovery_case with P3 rwb-case. The Work Package gives AC1 and AC3 of the legacy key to RWB-P1-DM009-APP, and no source says who performs the load into rwb_debtsale or how P1 reaches it without a cross-schema write; the ITG slice of the same key states that P1's own cutover migration loads the records, which contradicts the table ownership.
evidence: Ownership Map: debt_sale_lot owner S6 (basis Architecture v5 slide 41 and TSD S6 v2 T3.1); debt_sale_account owner S6; recovery_case owner P3. Legacy RWB-DM-009 Data table lists the same three tables. RWB-ITG-DM009-ITG section 1: the real lot and account records are loaded by P1's own cutover migration on its own Flyway sequence.

title: The extract and handover formats, the field list beyond AC1, the ON_CHANGE recency proof and the ten-day record are not specified beyond the AC wording
source: Legacy RWB-DM-009 AC1, AC3, Data table and Endpoints; FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 (DP09) and A2.14.2; Architecture v5 slide 32 (one-off bulk work); TSD P1 v3 T3.3 views 1 and 2
section: Legacy RWB-DM-009; FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 and A2.14.2; Arch v5 slide 32
description: AC1 requires each lot to keep its cut-off date, segment, reserve price and buyer and each account link to carry an account_key, and AC3 requires ten clean days and a sign-off, but no source gives the extract's source (dump, file or API), its format, where the package is held, the field list the package carries beyond the AC wording, or where the ten day count and the sign-off are recorded. DP09 has no ACE source system and no freshness stamp, so no source says how the recency of an ON_CHANGE product is proved apart from the reconciliation rows. Architecture v5 slide 32 puts cutover loads through service APIs and forbids a schedule reading rwb_* schemas.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-009 AC1: the migration reads them, and no balance and no payment is copied. AC3: ten clean days, then the data steward signs off. Endpoints: No endpoint in this story. FSD P1 v3 A2.14.2 product-to-source line: DP03, DP04, DP08, DP09, DP10, DP12, DP14 None; Workbench records, current on change. Architecture v5 slide 32: one-off bulk work through the P1 and P8 APIs, never their schemas.
proposed: Read the extract once through the cutover run from the legacy dump, land nothing in rwb_source_data, hand one package per cutover business date to rwb-debtsale, count the clean days from reconciliation_result rows of the migrated records, and hold the count and the sign-off in the cutover record of the release pipeline.

title: Gap cited in B2-P1-008
description: Cited by _work/msr/editlog/B2-P1-008.md; see the story body for the missing value.
evidence: Citation in a Stage B output
